claims.text: Formation of noble metal-based high-entropy alloy nanoparticles is governed by the balance between constituent enthalpies of mixing and surface energies.
The target multimetal nanoparticle system contains more than five interacting elements.
Changing composition changes the balance between enthalpy of mixing and surface energy.
Enthalpy of mixing mediates the structural response of the multimetal nanoparticles.
Surface energy mediates the structural response of the multimetal nanoparticles.
Competition between enthalpy of mixing and surface energy determines whether a homogeneous alloy or phase-separated nanoparticles form.
Composition variation can produce successful formation of noble metal-based high-entropy alloy nanoparticles.
The resulting high-entropy alloy nanoparticles will retain substantial surface-atom exposure.
The proposed mechanism applies to multimetal nanoparticle systems containing more than five interacting elements.
The proposed mechanism does not apply to systems containing fewer elements.
The proposed mechanism does not apply to different types of materials.
If the proposed energetic balance does not govern formation, composition variation should cause no significant difference in alloy homogeneity or phase separation.
If the proposed energetic balance does not govern formation, composition variation should cause no significant difference in surface-atom exposure.
